short: The lead ship of the US Navy's primary class of guided missile destroyers, built around the Aegis combat system.
full:
Commissioned on 4 July 1991, USS Arleigh Burke (DDG-51) is the lead ship of her class of guided missile destroyers. Designed around the Aegis Combat System and the SPY-1 passive electronically scanned array radar, it represented a revolution in naval anti-aircraft and anti-missile warfare. The ship was also the first US Navy destroyer built with stealth characteristics, shaping its steel superstructure to reduce its radar cross-section.

The Arleigh Burke class has become the backbone of the United States Navy's surface fleet, with over seventy vessels built. Capable of simultaneous anti-air, anti-surface, and anti-submarine warfare, these destroyers form the protective screen for carrier strike groups and conduct independent maritime operations worldwide. The lead ship remains in active service, having received numerous technological upgrades to its combat systems over its lengthy career.
